A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SANODEP research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and corresponding material can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original dynamical-system prediction and Bayesian-optimization experiments in Section 6, plus loss comparisons, parameter estimation and cross-domain experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original prediction and Bayesian-optimization results, including context-size evaluations, an encoder ablation and expanded parameter-estimation experiments in Sections 6–7 and Appendices D–E.

M1.justification: v1 uses the original SANODEP loss for PI-SANODEP; v2 explicitly adds a likelihood term for known system parameters, introducing direct parameter supervision (Appendix E.1). Algorithm 2 also corrects the post-observation time bound to include the delay. The base SANODEP encoder and two-scenario objective remain unchanged apart from terminology.

E1.justification: v2 removes the chemical reaction-network BO benchmark and extends parameter-estimation evaluation beyond two-dimensional Lotka–Volterra to the other five kinetic systems. The six main prediction benchmarks and GP-vector-field cross-domain scenarios remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds SANODEP without initial-condition augmentation and includes NODEP in forecasting comparisons. Its BO plot adds NP with lambda=0 and no longer identifies a PI-SANODEP curve, despite retained prose claiming PI results are reported (v1 Figure 2; v2 Figure 4). The alternative-ELBO comparator study is removed; the core GP, NP and NODEP families remain.

E3.justification: Reported context-trajectory ranges change from 1–20 to 0–10, and maximum within-trajectory context points decrease from 15 to 10. GP evaluation increases from 1,000 to 5,000 trajectories. v2 introduces evaluation across context sizes and changes several hypervolume reference points substantially (v1 Table 6; v2 Table 4), preventing direct interpretation of changed scores as same-setting gains.

E4.justification: v2 adds an initial-condition augmentation ablation and systematic context-size sensitivity analyses, plus a BO progression case study and broader parameter-recovery diagnostics. Conversely, v1 Appendix C.3's comparison of conditional and unconditional prior/ELBO variants is removed. Activation-function and GP-prior generalization analyses remain.

E5.justification: BO repetitions decrease from 20 to 10 random seeds, and the BO figure changes from medians with interquartile ranges to means with standard deviations. Five model-training seeds remain specified. This changes the BO statistical reporting without introducing a broader statistical methodology.

E6.justification: Prediction and BO results are extensively revised. For example, Table 1's Lotka–Volterra interpolation MSE for SANODEP changes from 51.1±16.8 to 32.1±0.55, both scaled by 10^-2, under revised sampling settings. v2 adds separate forecasting/interpolation results, context-size curves and parameter-recovery findings, while removing reaction-network and alternative-loss results.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the opening ELBO factorization, removes the alternative ELBO formulations and finite-sample Monte Carlo corollary, and qualifies Monte Carlo monotonicity as asymptotic. It also formulates the joint state/parameter likelihood for PI-SANODEP. The principal search-space proposition and core SANODEP derivation remain.

C1.justification: v2 removes the novel multi-scenario loss from the abstract and enumerated contributions, while retaining the loss itself. Parameter estimation, already claimed in v1, receives greater emphasis through its extended training objective. The central system-aware encoder and constrained two-stage BO contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the inverse-initial-value nonuniqueness rationale with a partial-observation argument, qualifies loss-mixing benefits as modest, and explains GP competitiveness through context abundance. It explicitly limits use on arbitrary systems without kinetic knowledge and adds discussion of PI-SANODEP initialization instability and difficulty estimating many parameters. These substantially refine mechanisms and applicability.

D1.justification: v2 documents PI-SANODEP parameter clipping, SIRD parameter ranges, Brusselator training duration and epidemiological BO initial-state mappings. However, it removes Selkov's equations and training distributions despite retaining its results. The code-access information, main architecture specifications, solver tolerances, hardware and timing table remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds BO background references and Cranmer et al.'s simulation-based inference work, removes citations associated with discarded loss-comparison, attention and reaction-network material, and reframes the comparison with Jiang et al. around irregular sampling. The overall positioning as a NODEP-derived approach to few-shot dynamical-system BO remains.

P1.justification: The introduction and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten, with question-based result discussions and separate prior-strength subsections. Appendices are regrouped, notation is revised, and 'multi-scenario' becomes 'bi-scenario.' These are substantial language and structural changes beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 changes typography and text width, adds BO overview, context-size and parameter-estimation graphics, reorganizes result tables into forecasting/interpolation blocks, and redraws prediction plots. The BO display changes from a seven-problem grid to six panels in one row. Existing diagrams and the runtime table are retained with relocation or reformatting.

improvement.justification: v2 better supports its central few-shot argument through context-size evaluations and a direct augmentation ablation, while explaining applicability limits more clearly. The net gain is modest because it removes the reaction-network and loss-variant studies, halves BO repetitions, and omits Selkov's training specification.
